p01.why: declared_only is declared and used but no unit defines it, so linking fails.

p02.why: The loop can be removed under -O2, but the exit status 7 is observable and is kept, so the run ends with nonzero status.

p03.why: Every volatile read and write happens in order at -O2, so port reaches 1000 and main returns 0.

p04.why: Each unit has its own internal-linkage local, so local() gives 1 and other() gives 2, the sum is 3, and main returns 0.

p05.why: p05.cpp has no declaration of defined_elsewhere, and each unit sees only its own declarations, so the use is not valid in that unit.

p06.why: A program must not take the address of main.

p07.why: f(1) is a constant, but f(0) dereferences a null pointer during constant evaluation, which is undefined, so the second static_assert is rejected.

p08.why: f is never called because z is 0, and f is not constant-evaluated outside a context that needs a constant, so main returns 0.

p10.why: main must have no parameters or exactly int and char**; a first parameter of type long is not allowed (EDG reportedly accepts it, Q-0112).

p11.why: The volatile writes happen in order, the last write stores 123, and the volatile read gives 123, so main returns 0.

p12.why: main must not be a template.

p13.why: A program must not call main.

p14.why: Control reaches the end of main, so the exit status is zero.

p15.why: f(0) divides by zero during constant evaluation, so the static_assert is not a constant and is rejected.

p17.why: argc is at least 1 (assumed: the runner passes the program name) and argv[argc] is a null pointer, so main returns 0.

p18.why: The unit compiles, but a program with no main does not link.

p19.why: sq gives 9 in constant evaluation and at run time, so main returns 0.

p20.why: if consteval picks 1 in the static_assert and 2 at run time, so both checks pass and main returns 0.

p21.why: The unit compiles (no -Werror, so the unused variable at most gives a warning), but there is no main, so it does not link.

p22.why: Constant evaluation of f() reaches 1 / 0, which is undefined, and is rejected even though the result is not used.

p23.why: main returns 3, which is a nonzero exit status.

p24.why: -Wall gives an unused-variable warning and -Werror turns it into an error; the spec only shows this warning indirectly, in the ATTR-6 evidence text.

p25.why: Initializing an int from a string literal is not valid, and TR-1 says this is rejected even in a function that is never called; no rule I found says a pointer does not convert to int implicitly.

p26.why: Initializing an int from a string literal is not valid; the spec has no explicit rule against pointer-to-integer implicit conversion, so this is a best guess from CONV-P3.
